name: GraphQL
description: Base module for integrating GraphQL with Drupal; exposes your Drupal data model through configurable GraphQL schemas and endpoints.
library_dependencies: webonyx/graphql-php (^15.32.3) — the underlying PHP GraphQL server/executor
provides_config_entities: graphql_server (config_prefix graphql_servers; each entity = one schema bound to one HTTP endpoint path)
provides_route_defaults: _graphql (marks a route as a GraphQL endpoint; RouteProvider mints graphql.query.<server_id> per graphql_server entity from its endpoint path)
provides_base_classes: Drupal\graphql\Plugin\GraphQL\SchemaExtension\SdlSchemaExtensionPluginBase (adds SDL + resolvers to a composable schema)
provides_drush_commands_list: graphql:dump (DumpSchemaCommand) — dump a server's schema to disk
graphql:detect-breaking-changes / graphql:breaking (DetectBreakingChangesCommand) — diff current schema vs. a previous dump
ecosystem_note: Developer FRAMEWORK for building GraphQL servers, not a turnkey feature. Depends on typed_data and bundles webonyx/graphql-php as the executor. The central object is the graphql_server config entity (config_prefix graphql_servers): each one names a Schema plugin, holds that schema's schema_configuration, and declares an HTTP endpoint path; RouteProvider then registers a POST/GET JSON route graphql.query.<id> at that path (controller RequestController::handleRequest). Building a schema means writing a Schema plugin (or, more commonly, using the ComposableSchema plus one or more SchemaExtension plugins) that pairs SDL (.graphqls type definitions) with resolvers wired via the ResolverBuilder/ResolverRegistry, where each field pulls data through DataProducer plugins (small reusable resolution steps). Introspection is on by default and there is an in-browser Explorer (GraphiQL) and Voyager per server under /admin/config/graphql. A bare install ships the plugin types + the server config entity but NO servers and NO usable schema — you either write one or enable the graphql_composable example submodule (schema id composable_example) for a working endpoint. Per-server access is governed by dynamically-generated permissions (execute <id> arbitrary/persisted graphql requests, use <id> graphql explorer/voyager) plus the global 'bypass graphql access'; a request with no matching permission is denied. This is the successor to the 3.x/4.x line; 4.x/5.x share the same architecture (config entity + SDL schema + data producers). 5.1.x keeps 5.0.x's architecture unchanged (info.yml version 5.1.0, same config schema and plugin types).
project_description:
This module lets you craft and expose a GraphQL schema for Drupal 10 and 11.

 It is is built around webonyx/graphql-php . As such, it supports the full official GraphQL specification with all its features.

 You can use this module as a foundation for building your own schema with lots of data producer plugins available and through custom code.

 For ease of development, it includes the GraphiQL interface at /graphql/explorer.

 Back to top 

 Example implementation 
 Example modules: https://git.drupalcode.org/project/graphql/-/tree/5.x/examples 

 Back to top 

 Resources 
 Documentation: https://drupal-graphql.gitbook.io/graphql/ 

Project homepage: https://www.drupal.org/project/graphql 

 Back to top 

 Upgrading from 4.x to 5.x 
 GraphQL 5.x has the same architecture as 4.x, the main differences are small PHP type API breaks. Upgrading is recommended, check the release notes .

 Back to top 

 Old 3.x version 
 The 3.x version of this module is now in maintenance mode.

 Differences to the 5.x and 4.x versions: the 3.x version automatically generates a GraphQL schema from Drupal entities and data structures. It exposes Drupal details over the GraphQL API. The 5.x version leaves the GraphQL schema design to the developer, which makes it easier to hide Drupal internal details. The 5.x version requires the developer to setup and map the GraphQL API schema.

 Check out https://github.com/drupal-graphql/drupal-decoupled-app for a complete example of a fully decoupled React and GraphQL 3.x application.

 Upgrading from 3.x to 5.x 
 We recommend upgrading from 3.x to 5.x to take advantage of the improvements made in the GraphQL module and the underlying GraphQL library. If you still require automatic generation of the schema then take a look at the GraphQL Compose or GraphQL Core Schema projects which have implemented automatic schema generation on top of the 5.x and 4.x GraphQL module.
